questions.question: How should the gap alert be wired in?

options.label: Standalone watchdog (Recommended)
options.description: Add a real data-truth check that queries GET /api/asset_prices/gaps and alerts if missing_count > threshold, run on its own cron (fold into / fix health_check.sh). Catches BOTH 'didn't run' and 'ran but no data' — the exact failure that went unnoticed for months.

options.label: Inside asset_report.sh
options.description: Check the gaps API right after the backfill step in asset_report.sh and alert if still behind. Simpler, but only fires when the daily run actually executes — won't catch a run that never fired.

options.label: Both
options.description: Watchdog cron for the 'didn't fire' case + an inline post-backfill check in asset_report.sh for 'ran but didn't catch up'. Most coverage, most surface area.

questions.question: Which email mechanism should the alert use?

options.label: send_deploy_email.py (Recommended)
options.description: Reuse the existing Gmail-SMTP helper. It reads the same encrypted mail.properties the asset report already decrypts, so creds are proven and no new config. HTML-capable.

options.label: mail CLI
options.description: Match health_check.sh's existing approach (the `mail` command to jdtogni@gmail.com). Minimal, but depends on a configured MTA on the box and is plaintext-only.

options.label: FamilyFund Laravel Mail
options.description: Add an alert endpoint/command on the FF side and have the watchdog trigger it, reusing ScheduledJobFailureMail-style mail. Keeps email logic in PHP but adds an API surface and crosses repos.

transcript_tail.text: I now have the full ticket. Let me nail down a few implementation-critical details: the git/submodule relationship of these scripts, how email is wired on the box (the `mail` CLI vs the Python SMTP helper), the `gaps` API response shape, and the cron setup.

Two important new finds: the scripts repo IS `dstrader-aws` (cloned locally as `dstrader-docker`), and FamilyFund already has a `ScheduledJobEmailAlertTrait.php`. Let me read that trait and the `gaps` endpoint to understand existing alert infrastructure.
FamilyFund already has scheduled-job failure alerting. Let me see the `gaps` endpoint response shape and where the alert trait is actually wired in.
Let me read the gaps endpoint response shape and how the alert trait is triggered in ScheduledJobTrait.
Let me check the existing reusable email helper on the box before proposing an approach.

I've now got the full picture. Here's what I found.

## The ticket
**"[Enhancement] Alert when the daily asset run / price backfill doesn't fire"** (board item `PVTI_lAHOBOqy7s4BYmISzgtni4o`, Todo, draft). Repo: `dstrader-aws` — which is exactly this `dstrader-docker` checkout (`origin → jdtogni78/dstrader-aws.git`). It's one of a 4-item gap cluster (one-time backfill, root-cause bug, widen self-heal window, **this alerting one**).

Core problem: the price pipeline was silently dead for 1–3 months. The scripts should self-report when prices don't land.

## What already exists

**dstrader side (shell):**
- `daily_run.sh` (cron `33 12 * * 1-5`) → runs `dstrader.sh` + `asset_report.sh`. **No success/failure alert.**
- `asset_report.sh:27` → runs `AssetReportRun gaps prod 30 NYSE` (detect+backfill, 30-day window) then posts positions/prices. **Result is only logged, never checked or alerted.** It also already calls `encr_files.sh decrypt` at the top, so `mail.properties` creds are live during the run.
- `health_check.sh` (cron `30 12 * * 2-6`) → greps yesterday's logs and emails via the `mail` CLI. Two weaknesses: it runs *before* the 12:33 daily run, and its success logic is a loose log-pattern grep, **not a data-truth check** (never verifies prices actually landed).

**FamilyFund side (PHP) — "the asset report already sends emails":**
- `GET /api/asset_prices/gaps?days=30&exchange=NYSE` → returns `{missing_count, missing_dates}`. This is the data-truth oracle.
- `ScheduledJobEmailAlertTrait::sendScheduledJobFailureAlert()` already emails on fund-report job failure (incl. stale-data exceptions). But it only fires **when a report is due** — so a mid-quarter multi-month gap goes unseen until report time. That's the hole this ticket fills.

**Email plumbing available:** `send_deploy_email.py` (Gmail SMTP, reads the same encrypted `mail.properties` the asset report already decrypts) and the `mail` CLI (what health_check uses).

## The key design insight
The *root cause* is "daily run didn't fire at all" — in which case `asset_report.sh` never executes, so any check embedded inside it also wouldn't fire. The most robust catch is an **external watchdog** that queries `GET /api/asset_prices/gaps` on its own cron and alerts if `missing_count` exceeds a threshold. That catches *both* "didn't run" and "ran but data didn't land," because in both cases prices are missing. `health_check.sh` is already the standalone-watchdog cron slot — it's the natural home.

Before I write code in the dstrader-aws repo, two scoping decisions:
